clue.text: Socks and shoes ultimately left behind gym near Victoria?

indicators.note: left behind says the letter from the shoes comes after the gym letters

parts.note: SW1 is the London postcode around Victoria station, written with the digit read as the letter I
PE, physical education, is school gym class

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word shoes

explanation.surface: Someone's socks and shoes have been forgotten at a gym close to Victoria station.
explanation.walkthrough: SW1 is the postal district around Victoria station in London; here the 1 is read as I. 'Socks' is a verb, not the clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To sock someone is to hit them hard, and swipes are sweeping blows, so both mean strikes.

clue.text: Unconventional duo — two characters originally making piece of artwork

indicators.note: unconventional means out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged
originally points to the opening letter of the word characters

explanation.surface: An offbeat pair, starting with just two letters, produce a work of art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconventional' shuffles DUO, TWO and C, the first letter of 'characters', the C coming from 'originally'.
explanation.definitionFit: A print made from a carved block of timber is a traditional form of graphic art.

clue.text: Old Scot has spoken about Independent magazine

parts.note: the Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland

indicators.note: about says the spoken word goes round the letter for Independent

parts.note: spoken means oral, said rather than written

explanation.surface: An ancient Scot is said to have talked about this very newspaper's magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' has ORAL wrapped round I.
explanation.definitionFit: A pictorial is a noun for an illustrated periodical, one built mainly from photographs.

clue.text: Feel annoyed about being taken in by children

indicators.note: being taken in by says the word for about goes inside the word for children

parts.note: seed in the old sense means offspring or descendants
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A parent gets irritated at being fooled by the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seed' for children is the biblical sense of offspring; 'being taken in by' is the containment signal, not about being fooled.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose one's temper or grow furious is an idiom built on the colour of anger.

clue.text: Book to travel around a S American city

indicators.note: around says the words to and travel are turned to read backwards

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A travel booking for a trip round a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns 'to travel' back to front as a pair of words, not just the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Colombia's capital stands high in the Andes of South America.

clue.text: Stick around one day in town down under

indicators.note: around says the stick word surrounds the day abbreviation

parts.note: a bat is a stick used to hit a ball
Thurs is the short form of Thursday, one day of the week

explanation.surface: Someone sticks around for a single day in an Australian town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' is the usual nickname for Australia; 'around' is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathurst is a city in New South Wales, Australia, famous for its motor race.

clue.text: Swallowed … swallowed by grey reptile

indicators.note: swallowed by says the eating word goes inside the grey abbreviation

parts.note: swallowed means ate, past tense of eat

explanation.surface: Something was swallowed, swallowed by a grey crocodile perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue repeats 'swallowed' with two jobs: first as a synonym, then 'swallowed by' as the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gater is an informal clipped form of alligator, the large American reptile.

clue.text: Short term employee has lots of time for painting

parts.note: a temp is a worker taken on for a short period
an era is a long span of time

explanation.surface: A temporary worker has plenty of free time to spend on art.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is painting with pigments bound in egg yolk, also the paintings made that way.

clue.text: He ran outside, unexpectedly not going inside

indicators.note: unexpectedly means in a surprising way, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A man suddenly ran out of the house rather than going in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unexpectedly' rearranges HE RAN OUTSIDE. The definition looks like a description of the runner but is about a pet's toilet habits.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet trained to relieve itself out of doors does not go indoors, the euphemism for messing in the house.

clue.text: Stock of tobacco policeman found in dingy hostels

indicators.note: found in says the policeman letters sit inside the other letters
dingy means shabby and run down, so the letters of hostels are knocked out of order

parts.note: PC stands for police constable

explanation.surface: A police officer discovers a hoard of tobacco in grubby lodging houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dingy' rearranges the letters of 'hostels' into SLOHEST, and 'found in' places the officer inside that jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the slop chest was the store of clothing and tobacco sold to sailors.

clue.text: Study noise of birds from part of Europe

parts.note: to scan is to examine or study closely
din is a loud noise
avian means of birds

explanation.surface: A researcher examines the racket made by birds from a region of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'birds' gives the adjective AVIAN, so 'of' is only the link.
explanation.definitionFit: Scandinavia is the northern region of Europe taking in Norway, Sweden and Denmark.

clue.text: Time to be part of system, possibly

indicators.note: to be part of says the answer is a run of letters lying inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A clock's timing might be one component of a wider system.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Time to be' as the definition, but tempo means time alone; 'to be part of' is the whole indicator. TEMPO runs across 'sysTEM POssibly'.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, tempo is the speed or time at which a piece is played.

clue.text: Locates different rooms nearby

indicators.note: different says the letters are arranged in another way

parts.note: quarters are rooms or lodgings

explanation.surface: An agent tracks down other rooms close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges LOCATES into AT CLOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes being very close together, within touching distance.

clue.text: Particular squad set out

definitions.meaning: a particular is a single item or point, as in going into particulars
a small group of soldiers or police given a special task
to set out in full, to describe item by item

explanation.surface: A specific team is sent out on a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Three separate definitions: a noun for an item, a noun for a team and a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for an item, a word for a task team, and a verb for listing fully all share this one word.

clue.text: Partisan, potentially one with ambition

indicators.note: potentially means in a possible form, so the letters may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: A political partisan may well be an ambitious type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' rearranges PARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who aspires to a position or success is striving after it.

clue.text: One soldier getting right drunk, do you say? Wrong

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an NCO is a non-commissioned officer

indicators.note: do you say signals that the word for drunk is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: wrecked is slang for very drunk

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether an inebriated soldier is right or wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do you say' means only the sound of the slang word for drunk counts, spelt here without its W, CK and ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something incorrect is mistaken, not true or accurate.

clue.text: Fifty ejected from Tallin bus travelling in foreign capital

indicators.note: travelling means moving around, so the letters are reshuffled once one is gone

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A traveller is thrown off a bus from Tallinn during a trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ejected from' removes L from TALLIN BUS, and 'travelling' rearranges what is left. Istanbul was the Ottoman capital, so 'capital' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul, as Constantinople, was long the capital of the Byzantine and Ottoman empires.

clue.text: Writer giving tally of minor celebs after a month

indicators.note: after says the list comes after the month

parts.note: Nov is short for November
the E-list is a jokey ranking of the least famous celebrities

explanation.surface: An author publishes a list of D-grade celebrities a month on.
explanation.walkthrough: The E-list is a joke extension of A-list down to the barely famous.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelist is an author of long prose fiction, one kind of writer.

clue.text: Victor Sharples, say, crosses unknown Italian location

parts.note: Vic is a short form of the name Victor

indicators.note: crosses says the soap name spans the unknown letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Ena Sharples was a famous character in the TV soap Coronation Street
z is a letter used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A man called Victor Sharples crosses an unknown spot in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Ena Sharples was the hairnetted gossip of Coronation Street, the long-running British TV soap. 'crosses' puts Z inside ENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicenza is a city in the Veneto region of northern Italy, known for Palladio's buildings.

clue.text: Shrub in areas full of prickly plants, with temperature dropping

indicators.note: full of says the two area letters hold the plants inside

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for area, so two areas give two As

indicators.note: dropping says the temperature letter is let go from the plant word

parts.note: cacti are spiny desert plants

explanation.surface: A bush grows in spots crowded with cacti, as the heat falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes temperature out of the plants, leaving CACI, which 'full of' then sets inside the two area letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Acacias are thorny shrubs and trees such as wattles, common in Australia and Africa.

clue.text: Bread and some butter served during tea

indicators.note: served during says the butter goes inside the tea word

parts.note: chai is a word for tea, especially spiced Indian tea
a pat is a small portion of butter

explanation.surface: Bread and a knob of butter are offered at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served during' is the containment signal; the tea is the Indian word, not the English one.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is an unleavened flatbread from India, cooked on a griddle.

clue.text: Carry off sailor over channel

indicators.note: over says, in this down answer, the sailor sits above the channel

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
a duct is a channel or tube

explanation.surface: A seaman is carried away over a stretch of sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channel' suggests the English Channel, but it is a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct someone is to take them away by force, to kidnap them.

clue.text: In vain reserve room left for royal aide

indicators.note: in says the next pieces are put inside the word vain

parts.note: ice means coldness of manner, reserve
a chamber is a room

explanation.surface: An official vainly holds back a room set aside for a royal helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In vain' reads as one phrase, but splits: 'In' is the containment signal and 'vain' is the container. Reserve as coolness of manner is the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vice-Chamberlain of the Household is a senior official of the British royal court.

clue.text: Suits, and where to pack them?

definitions.meaning: lawsuits, matters brought before a court

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads 'them' as clothes suits, while the first means legal suits.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal actions are court cases, and luggage for clothes is suitcases, the same word.

clue.text: After reflection, Salvation Army has welcomed English woman

indicators.note: after reflection says the result is read back to front as in a mirror
has welcomed says the army letters take in the English letters

explanation.surface: Having thought it over, the Salvation Army takes in an Englishwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has welcomed' gives SENGA, and 'After reflection' turns it round; 'English woman' tempts as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a female first name, so stands for a woman.

clue.text: Frenchman's game incomplete very near a road, one in Paris

indicators.note: incomplete says the game's name loses its final letter

parts.note: boules is the French game of bowls

explanation.surface: A French bowls game is cut short beside a road in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts the S from BOULES. 'one in Paris' refers back to 'road': a Paris road.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is famous for its broad tree-lined avenues, the grand boulevards of Haussmann.

clue.text: Mother's accompanying the Spanish girl

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother; with the s it is the possessive
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A mother goes along with a Spanish girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old or literary word for a young woman.

clue.text: Lacking order, we hear, for vegetable

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: tatty means scruffy and untidy, lacking order

explanation.surface: Something said to be messy turns out to be a vegetable.
explanation.walkthrough: TATTIE is the Scots word for a potato.
explanation.definitionFit: A potato is a vegetable, and this is its Scottish and northern dialect name.
